comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C4, C47, C52-C64) regarding Notch signaling requirement for CB NB elimination. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong experimental validation across multiple approaches. Reviewers describe evidence as 'solid' and 'clearly described and mostly convincing.'

Strong agreement on Delta as the Notch ligand (C65-C75). OpenEval emphasizes ligand specificity with 11 claims, while peer review groups this with additional claims about Delta sources (C8, C9, C76, C77, C81). Both find evidence SUPPORTED and accept Delta identification as solid contribution.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R3 addresses tissue-specific Delta sources (C76-C81), while peer R2 includes some of these claims (C76, C77, C81) alongside ligand identification claims. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review treats ligand identity and source together.

Perfect agreement on temporal requirement claims (C82-C84). Both evaluate temperature-shift experiments showing early Notch requirement. OpenEval also includes C119 (model claim). Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer reviewer explicitly validating the temporal window findings.

Strong agreement on early temporal factor defects (C85-C93). OpenEval focuses on prolonged Cas/Svp expression, while peer R4 includes these plus late temporal factor claims (C94-C99, C121). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer notes effects in ~20-40% of NBs.

Partial overlap on late temporal factor defects (C94-C99). OpenEval R6 focuses on late factors and temporal boundaries, while peer R4 combines early and late temporal patterning defects. Both find SUPPORTED, accepting that temporal patterning progression is affected.

Perfect agreement on cell cycle rescue experiment (C100-C103). Both evaluate dp110 rescue showing growth/cell cycle is not primary cause. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts this as supporting data ruling out alternative explanations.

Strong agreement on genetic rescue experiments (C104-C110). OpenEval emphasizes Imp knockdown and E93 overexpression rescues. Peer R5 focuses on C107-C110 (forcing temporal progression restores timing). Both find SUPPORTED as valid mechanistic evidence.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R8 addresses rescue experiments (C104-C110), while peer R9 focuses on characterization of ectopic NBs (C104-C105). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer accepts characterization as part of temporal patterning defect phenotype.

Strong agreement on Imp-Delta regulatory relationship (C111-C114). OpenEval notes convergence of bioinformatic and experimental data. Peer R6 includes these claims plus Syp/E93 regulation (C115-C117) and model claims. Both find SUPPORTED, accepting the feedback mechanism.

Partial overlap on late temporal factors regulating Delta (C115-C117). OpenEval R10 focuses on Syp/E93 reducing Delta-GFP. Peer R6 combines this with Imp regulation as part of broader feedback model. Both find SUPPORTED though mechanism (direct vs. indirect) not established.

Significant disagreement in evaluation type. Both address model/synthesis claims (C118, C120, C137). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with coherent mechanistic model. Peer finds UNCERTAIN, noting 'mechanistic insights are limited' and study is 'descriptive and lacks mechanistic explanation' for direct Notch regulation.

Agreement on uncertainty for broad claims. Both address C122 (speculative claim about Notch function). OpenEval finds overall model SUPPORTED but notes C122 is speculative. Peer finds UNCERTAIN for C39 and C122, questioning whether Notch directly regulates temporal genes.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R11 synthesizes findings into model (C118-C122). Peer R3 addresses temporal requirement (C82-C84, C119). Both find their respective claims SUPPORTED, though peer R3 focuses on experimental validation while R11 addresses model synthesis.

Strong agreement on background knowledge. OpenEval R12 covers extensive background (C1-C3, C17-C37, C48-C51). Peer R10 includes most of these plus Notch background (C38, C40-C42). Both find SUPPORTED as established field knowledge providing necessary context.

Partial overlap on Notch background. OpenEval R13 addresses Notch signaling background (C38-C42) including novel finding C39. Peer R10 includes some Notch background claims as part of broader context. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED; peer accepts background but questions C39 mechanism elsewhere.

Disagreement on novel finding C39. OpenEval R13 finds C39 (Notch regulates temporal decisions) SUPPORTED as primary finding. Peer R11 finds UNCERTAIN, noting unclear whether Notch directly regulates temporal genes or effects are indirect.

Perfect agreement on prior work context (C43-C46). Both evaluate authors' previous publication findings. Both find SUPPORTED as appropriately cited established context. Peer explicitly notes authors are 'building on their previous work.'

Partial overlap on broader significance. OpenEval R15 addresses neurogenesis termination significance (C15-C16). Peer R13 includes these plus mammalian comparative context (C138-C143). Both find SUPPORTED, accepting relevance to developmental neurobiology field.

OpenEval R16 addresses potential mechanisms discussion (C123-C127) synthesizing established knowledge with open questions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriately acknowledging uncertainties while providing context.

Minimal overlap on feedback model. OpenEval R17 integrates established knowledge with current findings to propose feedback model (C128-C131). Peer R6 includes some model claims (C129, C131) as part of broader regulatory relationship evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED for the regulatory relationships.

Minimal overlap on integration model. OpenEval R18 synthesizes multiple signaling inputs model (C132-C137). Peer R7 includes C137 as part of broader mechanistic evaluation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED; peer finds UNCERTAIN due to limited mechanistic insights.

Strong agreement on mammalian comparative context (C138-C143). Both evaluate broader relevance to mammalian systems with appropriate citations. Both find SUPPORTED, accepting the comparative discussion and identification of open questions about Notch in mammalian temporal patterning.
